name: Atezolizumab + Bevacizumab (atezolizumab / bevacizumab)
cyclesNote: Repeat every 21 days. Advanced/unresectable disease: continue until progression or unacceptable toxicity. Adjuvant high-risk resected setting: give for a defined fixed duration (about 1 year / 17 cycles) per the resected-disease approach. Endoscopy to screen and treat esophageal varices before starting because of the bevacizumab bleeding risk.

institution.provenance: ONCQIS grounded Standard Protocol (experimental, owner/device test only; not clinically activated)

supportiveCare: Screen for and manage esophageal varices by upper endoscopy before starting (bevacizumab bleeding risk).
Immune-related adverse event monitoring across organ systems; counsel prompt symptom reporting.
Blood pressure and urine protein monitoring (anti-VEGF component).
monitoring: thyroid, liver, glucose for immune-related effects
symptom review for colitis, pneumonitis, hepatitis, endocrinopathy

doseModificationRules.condition: grade 2 or higher immune-related adverse event
doseModificationRules.text: Hold atezolizumab and manage with corticosteroids per immune-related adverse event guidance; permanently discontinue for severe or recurrent grade 3-4 events. Clinical review before rechallenge.

doseModificationRules.condition: significant bleeding, grade 3-4 hypertension, or nephrotic-range proteinuria
doseModificationRules.text: Hold or discontinue bevacizumab per labeling; clinical review required.

drugs.name: Atezolizumab
drugs.notes: Atezolizumab 1200 mg IV flat on day 1 every 21 days. PD-L1 checkpoint inhibitor backbone of the preferred first-line advanced-HCC doublet; also studied adjuvant after high-risk resection. Authored from standard practice (NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma; IMbrave150 / IMbrave050 supporting evidence).

drugs.name: Bevacizumab
drugs.notes: Bevacizumab 15 mg/kg IV on day 1 every 21 days, given with atezolizumab. Anti-VEGF antibody; screen and treat esophageal varices before starting and monitor blood pressure and proteinuria. Authored from standard practice (NCCN Hepatocellular Carcinoma; IMbrave150 supporting evidence).
